label: Parity: a feature-uniform demand for a reason why excludes a brute contingent truth (inference)
rule: Uniformity transfers the demand along the shared feature; the demand met excludes bruteness
meaning: The owner's parity argument, analyst formulation, attribution deferred. The stance requires a reason why the target exists (P1), its demand is uniform in a feature k (P3) on which the target and the accepted fact o agree (P2). So it requires a reason why o obtains. If it met its demand and accepted o, o would have a reason, so it is not a brute contingent truth. For the naturalist who rejects an unreasoned God, God's existence as a mere brute fact in the owner's wording (target God, o the contingent foundation), it excludes the brute-contingency rival. This form concerns contingent o only: for a necessary o it holds vacuously, so the symmetric form is the stronger sibling (no reason at all, contingent or not). It establishes neither B2 nor that anything has a reason, it does not answer whether there is evidence for God, and it binds only stances that hold P1, P2 and P3 for one feature.
